I didn't find an official Cloudflare command-line chat client for the Agents SDK in these results. The closest material shows how to build one yourself.

**The Agents SDK client supports Node.js.** Cloudflare's Client SDK docs say you can connect to agents from browsers, Node.js, Deno, Bun, or edge functions — using WebSockets or HTTP. It exposes `AgentClient` and `agentFetch`, and it offers two ways to connect with a WebSocket connection, and one way to make HTTP requests. A terminal client would therefore run on Node and use one of these. The docs also mention `useAgent`, which is a React hook, so it's not the right fit for a plain terminal app.

**A terminal chat loop is a standard pattern.** The Composio guides don't use the Cloudflare Agents SDK. They wire an OpenAI or Claude agent to a Cloudflare MCP server, but their chat loops show the general approach. One uses Node's `readline` module with a `You:` prompt on stdin and stdout. The other is a Python loop that reads input, sends it to the agent, and streams the reply until the user types `exit` or `quit`. You could adapt either pattern so the input goes to an `AgentClient` WebSocket connection instead.

**Getting started:** Cloudflare's docs recommend the starter template, npm create cloudflare@latest agents-starter -- --template=cloudflare/agents-starter, which gives you a deployed agent to test against. You can also add the package to an existing Workers project with `npm i agents-sdk`.

If you want, I can run a narrower search for a specific runtime, such as Node-based `AgentClient` examples or a Cloudflare-published CLI for chatting with agents.

content.text:
I couldn't find an official Cloudflare tool for chatting with an Agents SDK agent from the terminal. You can build one easily, though. The Agents [Client SDK](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/communication-channels/chat/client-sdk/index.md) runs in Node.js, Deno and Bun as well as browsers. It provides `AgentClient` for WebSocket connections and `agentFetch` for HTTP requests. A small Node `readline` loop that sends each line to `AgentClient` and prints the reply makes a working CLI chat. The new [`cf` CLI](https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-cf-cli-launch/) is a different tool: it manages the Cloudflare API and doesn't chat with your agents. For a deployed agent to test against, use the [agents-starter template](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/index.md).

Sources:
- [Client SDK docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/communication-channels/chat/client-sdk/index.md)
- [Cloudflare Agents docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/index.md)
- [Introducing cf: the agentic CLI](https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-cf-cli-launch/)
